variant: Airbus A220-300 (BD-500-1A11), PW1500G, clean, gear down, static on ground
status: exterior-reference-reviewed; visual acceptance pending owner review

references.title: A220 Aircraft Characteristics Publication, Oct 2026, module BD500-3AB48-13800-00
references.author: Airbus
references.license: Public manufacturer document; local study only
references.scope: Tables of general dimensions and ground clearances. The dimension figures render with labels only, no line art, so locators were identified by label position. Visibility figure: eye 8 ft 6 in (2.6 m) aft of the nose tip; table 9 BL 20 in; 17 degrees down, 25 up.

references.title: airBaltic CS300 YL-CSA at Schiphol, pic2
references.author: Alf van Beem
references.license: Public domain; reference only, no pixels embedded
references.scope: Near-orthographic side view, traced at 43.65 px/m for the fuselage, fin, doors and windows. Livery ignored.

calibration: 43.65 px/m from the 38.69 m length, confirmed by the 15.31 m wheelbase (668 px). Heights rebased to locators A and R.

comparisons: Side render stacked above the same photograph at matching scale and inspected. No per-pixel overlay was made.
corrections: Row width corrected from 3.5 to 3.72 m (locator B) and height from 11.5 to 11.65 m (locator R, 11.58 to 11.73 m).
Static attitude 0.477 degrees nose down taken directly from locator AA.
Nose rows widened after the photograph showed the first pass too pointed in plan.
Reading M, J, G, F as wing stations gives 111.4 m2 of planform against the published 112.3 m2.
Seated eye moved from u 3.40 to the published 2.60. The window top is lowered from 2.8 to 2.71, because on this elliptical section the old top carried the glass over the pilot's head.

Kit changes: glass clear from the seat and tinted from outside, as on the Bendy airliner. The thick glareshield slab and its large FLIGHT GUIDANCE lettering are replaced by a thin sloped hood with a rolled lip over a slim mode control strip. The panel, floor and overhead take their reach from the nose skin, and a dark coaming lines the inside of the nose.
Published eye stations for four kit types sit 0.8 m ahead of where the kit had put them, and the same bias was removed here.

limitations: No plan or front drawing was usable: planform rests on locator interpretation, and locators other than those listed are unidentified.
Near wing and winglet in the photograph disagree with the planform by about 1.5 m, attributed to camera yaw and parallax but not resolved.
Exterior only: shared interior, refitted but not compared with an A220 flight deck.
The window top is 0.1 m under the airBaltic photograph's side window: chosen to give the pilot about the published upward view on a section rounder than the real one.
Sanity pass only: seating, glass and visibility. The panel, hood and pedestal remain the shared kit interior fitted to the nose, not compared with this type's real flight deck.
